question:
Find the median of the following data.

 
 

 Class Interval
 0-20
 20-40
 <td style="te
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cumulative Frequencies: 9, 25, 49, 64, 68.

Total frequency N = 68 ⇒ N ÷ 2 = 34.

The first cumulative frequency > 34 is 49, hence the median class is 40-60.

Median = l + [(N/2 − CF) ÷ f] × h

Median = 40 + [(34 − 25) ÷ 24] × 20 = 40 + (9 ÷ 24) × 20 = 47.5

**∴ The correct answer is 47.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Class Intervals: 0-20, 20-40, 40-60, 60-80, 80-100

Frequencies: 9, 16, 24, 15, 4

**Formula Used:**

Median = l + [(N/2 − CF) ÷ f] × h

Where:

l = lower limit of median class

N = total frequency

CF = cumulative frequency of the preceding class

f = frequency of the median class

h = class size

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, let us construct the cumulative frequency (CF) distribution:

⇒ 0-20: 9

⇒ 20-40: 9 + 16 = 25

⇒ 40-60: 25 + 24 = 49

⇒ 60-80: 49 + 15 = 64

⇒ 80-100: 64 + 4 = 68

⇒ Total frequency (N) = 68 ⇒ N ÷ 2 = 68 ÷ 2 = 34

⇒ The cumulative frequency just greater than 34 is 49, corresponding to the class 40-60.

⇒ Median class = 40-60

⇒ Here, l = 40, CF = 25, f = 24, h = 20

⇒ Median = 40 + [(34 − 25) ÷ 24] × 20

⇒ Median = 40 + (9 ÷ 24) × 20

⇒ Median = 40 + (3 ÷ 8) × 20

⇒ Median = 40 + (60 ÷ 8)

⇒ Median = 40 + 7.5 = 47.5

**∴ The correct answer is 47.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mode of Grouped Data

Mode = l + [(f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)] × h, where f₁ is the modal class frequency, f₀ is the preceding class frequency, and f₂ is the succeeding class frequency.

Mean of Grouped Data

Mean = Σ(fᵢxᵢ) ÷ Σfᵢ, where xᵢ represents the class mark or midpoint of each interval, calculated as (lower limit + upper limit) ÷ 2.

Empirical Relationship

Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean. This formula is highly useful to find one of the measures of central tendency when the other two are known for a moderately skewed distribution.
